parole.testo: From French bled, from Algerian Arabic, from Arabic بِلَاد (bilād).

parole.significato: An Algerian dish, a stuffed pastry roll
parole.testo: Borrowed from French bourek, borrowed from Algerian Arabic بوراك (būrāk), borrowed from Ottoman Turkish بورك (börek). See also brik, burek, byrek, borek.

parole.significato: The ruler of the Regency of Algiers (now Algeria) under the Ottoman Empire.
parole.testo: From French dey, from Algerian Arabic داي from Ottoman Turkish دایی (modern Turkish dayı).

parole.significato: A loose-fitting, ankle-length hooded robe worn by men in North Africa.
parole.testo: From French djellaba, from Algerian Arabic جلابة (jallāba).

parole.significato: A large desert region of sand dunes with little or no vegetation, especially in the Sahara.
parole.testo: From French erg, from Algerian Arabic, from Arabic عِرْق (ʕirq).

parole.significato: An Algerian Muslim who fought with the French during Algeria’s war of independence from 1954-1962; loosely, an Algerian…
parole.testo: Borrowed from French Harki, from Algerian Arabic حركي (ḥarkī), from حركة (ḥarka, “military operation”) (standard Arabic حركة (ḥaraka, “movement”)).

parole.significato: A red, spicy sausage from North Africa, made with lamb or beef.
parole.testo: From French merguez, from Algerian Arabic مرقاز (margāz).

parole.significato: A plundering and destructive incursion; a foray; a raid.
parole.testo: Borrowed from French razzia, from Algerian Arabic غَزِيَّة (ḡaziya), equalling Arabic غَزْوَة (ḡazwa, “raid, military campaign”). Doublet of ghazwa.

parole.significato: A form of music, originating in Oran, Algeria from Bedouin shepherds.
parole.testo: From French raï, from Algerian Arabic راي (rāy, “opinion”), from Arabic رَأْي (raʔy, “opinion”).
